text:
amanda_support: Customer ACME (acct: acme-inc) flagged a large variance — dashboard shows ~92k served tokens but invoice (INV-2026-0342) billed ~118k tokens for Mar 9-11. Customer is disputing ~28% overage. They provided short examples and are asking for a breakdown. :exclamation:

amanda_support: Linking their example trace IDs: r_8a1f, r_8a2b. They say most calls are short prompts (~12-40 tokens) with repeated prefixes (system prompt + small user prompts).

priya_billing: Thanks Amanda. Can you attach the invoice CSV and meter export for that invoice window? I want the raw metering lines for those trace IDs.

amanda_support: Uploaded meter export snippet and invoice rows to the ticket: https://redwood.support/t/INV-2026-0342 (private link). Quick paste of the meter lines for r_8a1f:
```
metering_event,timestamp=2026-03-10T14:02:13Z,trace=r_8a1f,billed_tokens=184,served_tokens=26,model=gpt-open-7b,route=/v1/chat
```

josh_eng: Whoa — billed 184 but served 26. That screams batching/prefix accounting thing. Two common suspects: continuous batching + prefix/KV cache accounting double-counting, or the metering service consuming a different tokenization config.

josh_eng: @dave_research can you check whether runtime emitted any prefetch/kvcache events for those requests? Also please check the batching window that day (we had a burst at ~14:01 UTC).

dave_research: Looking now. I pulled runtime trace for r_8a1f. We have these events (condensed):
```
2026-03-10T14:02:12.998Z runtime:receive request id=r_8a1f len_prompt=22
2026-03-10T14:02:13.001Z batch:attached batch_id=b_20260310_1402 window_ms=8 requests=14
2026-03-10T14:02:13.005Z kvcache:prefetch prefix_hash=0x9f3 len_prefix=16 cache_hit=true
2026-03-10T14:02:13.010Z runtime:emit served_tokens=26
2026-03-10T14:02:13.011Z metering:record billed_tokens=184 batch_accounting=true
```

josh_eng: That pattern matches a known edge: when continuous batching with prefix prefetch merges multiple request prefixes into an internal combined sequence, metering currently attributes the full expanded tokenized length (including repeated prefixes per request) to billed_tokens under batch accounting, but served_tokens reflects per-request served tokens after KV cache hits remove duplicated prefix generation. In short: billed includes the inflated combined size.

priya_billing: Is that a bug or expected behavior? Customer expects billed==served or at least an explanation.

josh_eng: This is a byproduct of our batching accounting model — historically we bill on the combined compute the cluster performed (which is what the billing pipeline ingests). With prefix/KV cache warm hits, compute may be less than naive combined token count, and served_tokens (what the API returned) will be smaller. However, the numbers here look high — 184 billed for a 26-token served reply with a 16-token prefix should not be that far off. Need to confirm: why 184 (not like 40-60)?

dave_research: Stepping deeper, the batch had 14 requests; most shared the same prefix but different small suffixes. The metering pipeline currently multiplies the full combined input (prefix counted per-request before KV deduction) across the batch. There's also an old safety margin factor for attention memory in the kernel selection path that adds tokens for internal re-ordering when optimizing kernels; that margin was set to +2 tokens per request, not enough to explain 184. I'm seeing an additional multiplier in the batching exporter that applies when "batch_accounting" flag is true: it records combined_input_tokens + combined_output_tokens + padding_tokens_for_alignment. For b_20260310_1402 that padding was sizable due to alignment to 128-token kernel thresholds. Combined_input_tokens=120, combined_output_tokens=40, padding=24 -> billed=184. But served sum was 26 across the request.

lena_product: So the invoice shows compute we actually used on the GPUs (with padding/alignment), while the API served tokens are what the customer saw. This is confusing to customers. We need a clear explanation and either a dashboard breakdown or a billing correction if it's wrong.

amanda_support: Customer expects either refund or a detailed breakdown per-call (they can accept billed compute if clearly explained). They want a quick repro so they can stop sending support escalations.

josh_eng: Immediate actions I recommend:
- Export full metering lines for invoice and group by batch_id (command below).
- Re-run a local replay against a dedicated dev runtime with continuous batching enabled to reproduce accounting delta.
- If reproduced, add a short-term statement to the customer explaining alignment/padding and batch-level billing.

josh_eng: Meter export query (internal):
```
curl -u $METER_API_KEY "https://metering.redwood.internal/v1/export?invoice=INV-2026-0342&format=csv" > inv-0342.csv
# then group by batch_id, sum billed/served
```

priya_billing: I pulled inv-0342.csv and grouped by batch_id. There are ~3 batch windows with large deltas. I can share an annotated CSV snippet in the ticket.

dave_research: For repro: script that spams short requests sharing a prefix with continuous batching ON. It reproduces billed >> served due to kernel alignment. Example (pseudo):
```
for i in $(seq 1 200); do
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/chat -H "Authorization: Bearer $DEV_KEY" -d '{"messages":[{"role":"system","content":"context: short"},{"role":"user","content":"quick q '$i'"}],"max_tokens":16}' &
  sleep 0.03
done
```
Run against dev runtime with BATCH_WINDOW_MS=8 and KERNEL_ALIGN=128 to reproduce.

infra_bot: Automated note: Ingress spike and batch window reduced to 8ms during incident window; kube autoscaler added 2 nodes at 14:03 UTC.

lena_product: Action item: put a prominent note in Billing FAQ explaining that billed tokens reflect GPU compute including batch-level padding/alignment and that served tokens are user-facing content tokens. Also add a dashboard breakdown showing batch_id-level billed vs served to help customers reconcile.

amanda_support: I'll respond to customer with an interim explanation and offer either a one-time credit or full CSV breakdown. Priya, please advise on credit policy for this pattern.

priya_billing: I'll escalate for review. If this is an unexpected regression (we didn't document alignment billing), we can offer partial credit for invoices in the window while eng investigates.

josh_eng: I'll open an eng-runtime ticket to: (1) mark this batching exporter behavior as 'surprising', (2) add a flag to emit both 'compute_billed' and 'per_request_approx_billed' and (3) add tests for kernel alignment accounting. Ticket: ENG-RUNTIME-4821.

dave_research: I'll reproduce locally and attach a short recording + metrics. If we can show consistent delta, we should consider changing exporter to attribute padding to a separate line item instead of inflating per-request billed tokens.

amanda_support: Thanks all. I'll post the customer-facing note draft in the ticket before EOD. :thumbsup:

priya_billing: Assigned to billing review. Priya -> will follow up tomorrow with policy and whether to credit invoice INV-2026-0342.

josh_eng: tagging @lena_product for visibility on docs and @dave_research for repro artifacts. :eyes:
